question: What is the architectural style of the Brihadisvara temple in Tamil Nadu?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Brihadishvara** **Temple**:

 
 
• It was originally known as **Peruvudaiyar Kovil** and also called **Rajarajeswaram**.
 
• It is a **Hindu Dravidian-styled temple** dedicated to the **god Shiva** located on the South bank of the **Cauvery River** in **Thanjavur**, **Tamil Nadu**, India.
 
• The Brihadisvara Temple was built under **Raja Raja Chola**, a **Chola emperor** ruling over ancient Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is part of a group of Chola-era temples designated as a **World Heritage Site**. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gadaga** **architectural style**:

 
 
• Influences of **Western Chalukya architecture** can be discerned in the geographically distant schools of architecture of the** Hoysala Empire** in southern Karnataka, and the Kakatiya dynasty in present-day Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Sometimes called the **Gadaga style of architecture**, Western Chalukya architecture is considered a precursor to the Hoysala architecture of southern Karnataka.
 
 
 
• **Nagara architectural style**:
 
 
• **Nagara Style of Architecture** is a Temple Style of Architecture prevalent in **North India**. The temple-style architecture of Indian states such as **Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Odisha, Assam, West Bengal, and Madhya Pradesh** are all included in Nagara Architecture.
 
 
 
• **Champa architectural style**:
 
 
• **Myson Temple** is a **Hindu Champa-styled temple** in Vietnam.
 
• It was constructed between the **4th and the 14th century** by the **Kings of Champa**, an Indianized kingdom of the Cham people.
 
• The temples are dedicated to the worship of the** god Shiva**, the most important of which is **Bhadreshvara**.
